svg.title: Figure 3. Anatomy of the stress-strain diagram
svg.desc: Two plots of an illustrative material, not the lab specimens. Part a, engineering stress in MPa versus engineering strain in percent from 0 to 34 percent for a mild steel: a steep linear elastic line up to an upper yield point near 360 MPa, a drop to a flat lower-yield Luders plateau near 340 MPa extending to about 2 percent strain, a rising strain-hardening curve to a maximum of about 500 MPa near 18 percent strain, then a shaded necking region where engineering stress falls to fracture at 32 percent. A dash-dot true-stress curve, plotted up to the maximum load only, lies above the engineering curve and keeps rising. Part b, aluminum-like curve with gradual yielding over 0 to 1.2 percent strain: a dashed line of slope E starting at 0.2 percent strain cuts the curve at the 0.2 percent offset yield strength, marked by a diamond near 250 MPa.
